title: the kbtools entry for backlog.py set cuts the list of options a batch refuses after --notes and runs into the next fragment
goal: the kbtools entry for backlog.py set names every option a batch of several ids refuses: --title, --goal, --notes, --repro, --repro-reason, --parent, --clause and --check, by wording the usage block of _tools/backlog.py so that no line of that sentence starts with -- (kbtools.subcommand_blocks skips such a line as an option line)

run:
import json,subprocess,sys
out=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbtools.py","--json","backlog.py set several ids"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout
b=" ".join(next(e for e in json.loads(out)["entries"] if e["tool"]=="backlog.py set")["answers"])
i=b.find("a batch refuses"); print(b[i:i+140])
sys.exit(0 if all(x in b for x in ("--repro-reason","--parent","--clause","--check")) else 1)

import json, subprocess, sys

b = " ".join(e["answers"])
i = b.find("a batch refuses")
seg = b[i:i + 400]
ok = i >= 0 and all(x in seg for x in ("--title", "--goal", "--notes", "--repro", "--repro-reason", "--parent", "--clause", "--check"))
print(ok); sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

The reviewer did not locate the cut in kbtools.py (subcommand_blocks and the description join): keep the continuation lines whole, or put the refused-options sentence on lines the excerpt keeps.
